items.informal_name: Exponential Little-o Inequality for $ r_1 < r_2 $
items.type: ∀ {r₁ r₂ : ℝ}, 0 ≤ r₁ → r₁ < r₂ → (fun n => r₁ ^ n) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => r₂ ^ n
items.informal_description: For non-negative real numbers $ r_1 $ and $ r_2 $ satisfying $ 0 \leq r_1 < r_2 $, the exponential function $ r_1^n $ is asymptotically negligible compared to $ r_2^n $ as $ n \to \infty $, i.e., $ r_1^n = o(r_2^n) $.

items.informal_name: Little-o Asymptotic for Power Functions with Exponents $ p < q $
items.type:
∀ {𝕜 : Type u_1} [inst : NormedField 𝕜] [inst_1 : LinearOrder 𝕜] [IsStrictOrderedRing 𝕜] [OrderTopology 𝕜] {p q : ℕ},
  p < q → (fun x => x ^ p) =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => x ^ q
items.informal_description: For any linearly ordered field $\mathbb{K}$ with a strict ordered ring structure and order topology, and for natural numbers $p, q$ satisfying $p < q$, the function $f(x) = x^p$ is asymptotically dominated by $g(x) = x^q$ in the little-o sense as $x \to \infty$. Specifically, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some $M \in \mathbb{K}$ such that $\|x^p\| \leq \varepsilon \cdot \|x^q\|$ holds for all $x \geq M$.

items.informal_name: Exponential Dominance: $ e^{a t} \cdot t^k = o(e^{b t}) $ for $ a < b $
items.type: ∀ (k : ℝ) {a b : ℝ}, a < b → (fun t => Real.exp (a * t) * t ^ k) =o[Filter.atTop] fun t => Real.exp (b * t)
items.informal_description: For any real numbers $ a < b $ and any real $ k $, the function $ f(t) = e^{a t} \cdot t^k $ is asymptotically negligible compared to $ g(t) = e^{b t} $ as $ t \to \infty $. This means $ \lim_{t \to \infty} \frac{e^{a t} \cdot t^k}{e^{b t}} = 0 $, demonstrating exponential growth with larger exponent $ b $ dominates any polynomial multiple $ t^k $ of an exponential with smaller exponent $ a $.

items.informal_name: x^s is Little-o of e^x at Infinity
items.informal_description: For any real number $ s $, the function $ x^s $ is asymptotically negligible compared to the exponential function $ e^x $ as $ x $ approaches infinity, i.e., $ x^s = o(e^x) $ as $ x \to \infty $.

items.informal_name: x^n is Little-o of e^x as x approaches Infinity
items.informal_description: For any natural number $ n $, the function $ x^n $ is asymptotically negligible compared to the exponential function $ e^x $ as $ x $ approaches infinity. Formally, $ x^n = o(e^x) $ with respect to the filter at infinity, meaning that $ \lim_{x \to \infty} \frac{x^n}{e^x} = 0 $.

items.informal_name: x^s is little-o of e^{bx} as x approaches infinity
items.type: ∀ (s : ℝ) {b : ℝ}, 0 < b → (fun x => x ^ s) =o[Filter.atTop] fun x => Real.exp (b * x)
items.informal_description: For any real number $s$ and positive real number $b$, the function $x^s$ is asymptotically negligible compared to the exponential function $e^{b x}$ as $x$ approaches infinity. This means that for every $\varepsilon > 0$, there exists some $M$ such that $|x^s| \leq \varepsilon |e^{b x}|$ for all $x \geq M$.

items.informal_name: Exponential Growth Dominates Polynomial Growth for $r > 1$
items.type: ∀ {R : Type u_2} [inst : NormedRing R] (k : ℕ) {r : ℝ}, 1 < r → (fun n => ↑n ^ k) =o[Filter.atTop] fun n => r ^ n
items.informal_description: For any natural number $k$ and real number $r > 1$, the function $n \mapsto n^k$ (interpreted in a normed ring $R$) is asymptotically negligible compared to the exponential function $n \mapsto r^n$ as $n \to \infty$. Specifically, $n^k = o(r^n)$ with respect to the filter at infinity, meaning that polynomial growth is dominated by exponential growth when the base of the exponential exceeds 1.

  0 < r → 0 ≤ᶠ[l] g → f =o[l] g → (fun x => f x ^ r) =o[l] fun x => g x ^ r
items.informal_description: If $0 < r$ and $g(x) \geq 0$ eventually in the filter $\mathcal{F}$, and $f(x) = o_{\mathcal{F}}(g(x))$, then $f(x)^r = o_{\mathcal{F}}(g(x)^r)$ for real exponentiation.
